narration.text: This burned scroll was too fragile to open. Scientists read it anyway. The En-Gedi scroll crumbled when it was touched. Researchers scanned it with X-rays, building a three-dimensional map. Inside that scan, they traced the surviving layers. In this scroll, the ink showed up more densely than the parchment. They mapped that signal onto digital surfaces, then flattened them into readable images. The recovered Hebrew text came from the Book of Leviticus. This worked because the ink was detectable in the scan. Different materials need different approaches. They revealed surviving writing without unrolling the fragile original.
